output.summary: KEP-5593 splits the per-node max CrashLoopBackOff delay knob out of KEP-4603 into its own KEP. Its status is implementable at stage beta, with a per-node config `crashloopbackoff.maxSeconds` that can lower the maximum backoff down to 1s.
output.rationale: The original KEP-4603 bundled a default-curve change and a configurable maximum, both in alpha. The split lets each part graduate separately, and this KEP tracks only the configurable maximum. Reviewers said the feature is stateless and that a rollback only requires updating the config and restarting kubelet. The sources do not say why the beta stage was chosen in this KEP, and a maintainer later asked whether there was enough soak time.

alternatives.option: Create a new KEP for the configurable maximum and leave KEP-4603 at alpha with everything (the original plan)
alternatives.why_not: Sergey Kanzhelev said: "Can we downscope the original KEP instead of creating a new one and keeping the other one in alpha already?" The sources do not record a final decision on this alternative.

alternatives.option: Also address the Success-state backoff (constant or instant backoff for Succeeded Pods)
alternatives.why_not: The KEP states: "This proposal will NOT change: * backoff behavior for Pods transitioning from the "Success" state differently from those transitioning from a "Failed" state".

alternatives.option: Complex heuristics in kubelet (system state, workload factors, anomaly detection)
alternatives.why_not: Non-goals: "This effort is purposefully NOT implementing more complex heuristics by kubelet" to focus on simpler, easily modeled changes.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes providing an option to cluster operators to configure a lower maximum backoff for all containers on a specific Node, down to 1s.
The PR https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5594 splits out those features into two separate KEPs so that we can track their graduation separately from now on.
Risk is that a configured crashloop backoff causes the kubelet to become unstable. If that happens, a rollback just requires updating the config and restarting kubelet.
do we have enough soak time? didn't it just go beta in 1.35?
